chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Hilal, from Uqbah ibn Khalid, from Abi Abd Allah عليه السلام, concerning a man who performed the night prayer and prayed the witr, then remembered that he had forgotten two rak'ahs of his prayer. How should he act? He said:
"He stands and prays the two rak'ahs that he forgot in their place, then he performs the witr."

Whoever forgets the tashahhud in a supererogatory prayer until he enters the third rak'ah, then remembers after the ruku', let him disregard the ruku', sit, recite the tashahhud, and say the taslim. But it is not like that in the obligatory prayer, because in the obligatory prayer, if he remembers that he did not recite the tashahhud after he has already performed ruku', he continues in his prayer; then he recites the tashahhud after the taslim and performs the two sajdahs of sahw. We have already explained this earlier, and that which indicates what we have said.

key_terms.التَّسْلِيمِ: the closing salutation ending the prayer
key_terms.التَّشَهُّدِ: the testimony recited in the sitting portion of salat (prayer)
key_terms.سَجْدَتَيِ السَّهْوِ: the two prostrations performed to remedy forgetfulness in prayer
key_terms.صَلَاةَ اللَّيْلِ: the night prayer performed as a supererogatory devotional act
key_terms.يُوتِرُ: he performs the witr prayer concluding the night prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he forgets part of the night prayer or the tashahhud in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This text gives rulings on forgetfulness in salat (prayer), especially in the night prayer and regarding omitted tashahhud. It distinguishes between nafilah and faridah, stating that the legal response differs depending on whether the prayer is supererogatory or obligatory. It also affirms the ruling of making up the missed tashahhud after taslim in the obligatory prayer together with sajdatay al-sahw.
